Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace, but with inflation still above target the FOMC’s decision to hold the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50 percent and continue balance-sheet runoff is consistent with rules- and forecast-based frameworks in the literature (e.g., Clarida–Galí–Gertler on policy rules and Svensson–Woodford on inflation-forecast targeting), the New Keynesian Phillips Curve emphasis on expectations, and the time-inconsistency/inflation-bias lessons that argue for patience until inflation is sustainably near 2 percent. The Committee’s view that risks are moving into better balance, alongside ongoing Treasury and agency MBS runoff that works through term-structure channels (as in Cochrane–Piazzesi), supports a mildly positive but cautious assessment.
